content.content: 1 # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. I re-graded the test files you listed against the spec. **Verdict: pass, 9/10 overall, no item under 8.** `npm test` passes 149/149 when I run it here. I took the 45-mutant result from your note and did not re-run it.

**Last round's fixes: all done.**
- **Harness helpers:** `server-harness.mjs` now has a labelled `assertError`, `stopServer` (waits for `'close'`), `chunkedPost` (handles back-pressure), a 10 s timeout on `startServer` that cleans up after itself, a timeout on `runToExit` that the test's own assertion reports, and a frozen `JSON_HEADERS`.
- **No fixed sleeps:** the only timers are the timeouts in the harness and in the smoke file.
- **Data-file tests:** `assertRejected` sits in `server.datafile.test.mjs` and is used for every rejected case.
- **Page tests:** the helpers now live in `page-harness.mjs`, `change` is sync, and `EXPECTED_FIELDS` is in place.
- **Invisible characters** are written as `\u` escapes, and the asserts inside loops have case labels.
- **Smoke file:** the two changed lines are correct. `runToExit` resolves on `'close'` (line 54), and line 234 uses `'\uFEFF{}'`.

**What I checked**
- **Spec values:** every spec message is compared exactly, and status, body and content type are checked together through `assertError`.
- **Boundaries:** the near-miss cases are good, e.g. 10000 vs 10001 bytes including multi-byte and chunked bodies, `trim` vs `trimEnd`, the `params.get` first-value rule, and PORT checked before the data file.
- **Test independence:** each test uses its own temp dir and an OS-picked port, and the tests for ports 3000 and 65535 are skipped when the port is busy.
- **Size:** files are 95–396 lines and the longest function is about 34 lines.
- **Leftovers:** no `console.log` or TODOs. The `catch { json = undefined }` blocks are deliberate (they mark a non-JSON reply), not swallowed errors.

**New findings (small, mostly duplication)**
- **404 loop:** the bad-ids loop in `server.routing.test.mjs` (lines 108–111) still checks status, body and content type by hand instead of calling `assertError`.
- **Big-body loop:** the loop at lines 157–159 of the same file checks status and body but not the content type, which `assertError` would also cover.
- **Harness reply parsing:** the code that collects and JSON-parses a reply appears three times in `server-harness.mjs`.
- **Page field values:** the same values are written out in three places in `page.behaviour.test.mjs`.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — one job per helper and test, shallow nesting, the table-driven cases read clearly
naming: 9 — clear names (`assertRejected`, `chunkedPost`, `EXPECTED_FIELDS`); `getRooms` is the one vague name for something that only asserts
duplication: 8 — one loop still checks by hand what `assertError` does; reply parsing is copied three times in the harness; page field values repeated
size: 9 — every file under 400 lines, every function under 35 lines
errors: 9 — timeouts end as labelled assertion failures, cleanup is deterministic, no swallowed errors
tests: 9 — exact equality on spec values, strong near-miss and boundary cases, mutants killed, deterministic, independent
security: 10 — no secrets; temp dirs created with mkdtemp and removed after each test
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.routing.test.mjs:108 replace the three hand-written asserts with `assertError(res, 404, 'booking not found', \`id ${id.slice(0, 20)}\`)`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.routing.test.mjs:158 replace the status and body asserts with `assertError(res, status, msg, name)` so the content type is checked too
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/helpers/server-harness.mjs:118 move the reply collect-and-parse code into one `readReply(res, resolve, reject)` helper, use it from `request` and `chunkedPost` (line 191), and reuse its JSON parse in `rawRequest` (line 158)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.behaviour.test.mjs:29 build `fill`'s defaults from `{ ...EXPECTED_FIELDS, title: 'T' }`, and at line 159 expect `{ ...EXPECTED_FIELDS, title: '  Plan <b>  ' }`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.rules.test.mjs:100 build `over` with a helper shared with `sizedBody` (e.g. a padding-by-char-count helper) instead of repeating the padding maths inline
